title: Embedded Systems
summary: Microcontrollers from the bit up. The first threshold is the memory-mapped register: hardware is controlled by writing bits to addresses. The second is the interrupt: the program is no longer the only thing deciding what runs next.
sources: Valvano: Embedded Systems: Introduction to ARM Cortex-M Microcontrollers

nodes.label: Binary, Hex & Bitwise Operations
nodes.summary: Setting, clearing, toggling and testing single bits with |, &, ~, ^ and shifts.
nodes.outcome: Set, clear, toggle and test bit n of a register without disturbing the others.
nodes.check: Write the expression that clears bit 3 of x and leaves every other bit alone.

nodes.label: "x & (1 << n) gives 1 or 0"
nodes.summary: A masked test yields 0 or 2ⁿ, not 1. Comparing it with == 1 fails for every bit except bit 0.
nodes.outcome: Write a correct bit test.
nodes.answer: 32 (0b00100000); the comparison is false. Test with != 0 instead.

nodes.label: Microcontroller Architecture
nodes.summary: CPU, flash for code, RAM for data, and peripherals (GPIO, timers, ADC, serial) on one chip, all sharing one address space.
nodes.outcome: Read a block diagram and say where code, variables and peripherals live.
nodes.check: Where does a global variable live, and where does the program's code live?
nodes.answer: The variable is in RAM (SRAM); the code is in flash.

nodes.label: Memory-Mapped Registers
nodes.summary: Peripherals appear as addresses: writing a bit turns on a pin, reading one reports a button. Once this lands, the datasheet becomes the manual for the whole chip.
nodes.outcome: Configure a peripheral from its datasheet register table.
nodes.check: On an AVR, which register makes PB5 an output, and which drives it high?
nodes.answer: Set bit 5 of DDRB to make it an output; set bit 5 of PORTB to drive it high.

nodes.label: GPIO: Inputs, Outputs & Pull-ups
nodes.summary: Pins configured as push-pull outputs or as inputs, with pull-up resistors so a released button reads a defined level.
nodes.outcome: Wire and read an active-low button with a pull-up.
nodes.check: A button connects the pin to ground, with a pull-up enabled. What does the pin read when pressed, and when released?
nodes.answer: 0 when pressed, 1 when released (active-low).

nodes.label: "An unconnected input reads 0"
nodes.summary: A floating CMOS input picks up noise and reads randomly; it needs a pull-up or pull-down.
nodes.outcome: Explain and fix a floating input.
nodes.check: A button pin with no pull resistor reads random values when released. Why?
nodes.answer: It floats: nothing drives it, so stray charge and noise decide the level. Add a pull-up or pull-down.

nodes.label: Non-Blocking Timing
nodes.summary: Compare elapsed time against a stored timestamp instead of waiting, so the loop stays responsive to everything else.
nodes.outcome: Blink an LED and read a button in the same loop without delay().
nodes.check: Why is `if (millis() - last >= 500)` preferred to `delay(500)`?
nodes.answer: It never stops the loop, so other tasks (buttons, sensors) keep running; delay() blocks everything.

nodes.label: "delay() is harmless"
nodes.summary: A blocking wait freezes every other job in the loop: inputs are missed and timing stacks up.
nodes.outcome: Find the missed-input bug caused by delay().
nodes.check: A loop calls delay(1000) and then reads a button. A 200 ms press happens during the delay. Is it seen?
nodes.answer: No: the button is only read between delays, so short presses are missed.

nodes.label: Switch Bounce & Debouncing
nodes.summary: Mechanical contacts chatter for milliseconds; firmware accepts a change only after the input has been stable for a while.
nodes.outcome: Write a debounced press counter.
nodes.check: A button bounces for 5 ms. A naive edge counter registers 7 presses for one push. What is the simplest fix?
nodes.answer: Accept a new state only after it has been stable for longer than the bounce (e.g. 20 ms).

nodes.label: Hardware Timers
nodes.summary: Counters clocked from the system clock through a prescaler, firing on overflow or compare match.
nodes.outcome: Compute a prescaler and compare value for a target period.
nodes.check: A 16 MHz clock with prescaler 64 drives a timer. How many ticks make 1 ms?

nodes.label: PWM
nodes.summary: Switch fast and vary the fraction of time on: the average sets LED brightness or motor speed.
nodes.outcome: Generate PWM at a given frequency and duty cycle.
nodes.check: A 5 V PWM signal at 25% duty drives an LED. What average voltage does it see, and why must the frequency be high?
nodes.answer: 1.25 V on average; above roughly 100 Hz the eye averages it instead of seeing flicker.

nodes.label: Interrupts & ISRs
nodes.summary: Hardware events pause the main program and run a handler. Troublesome because the main code can be interrupted between any two instructions.
nodes.outcome: Write a short ISR that sets a flag for the main loop.
nodes.check: Why should an interrupt service routine be short?
nodes.answer: While it runs, other interrupts and the main loop wait; long ISRs cause missed events and jitter.

nodes.label: "Variables shared with an ISR need nothing special"
nodes.summary: Without volatile the compiler may cache the variable in a register; multi-byte values can also be torn mid-read.
nodes.outcome: Share a counter between an ISR and main safely.
nodes.check: A main loop waits on a flag set by an ISR, but never sees it change. Likely cause?
nodes.answer: The flag is not volatile, so the compiler hoisted the read out of the loop.

nodes.label: Reading Sensors with the ADC
nodes.summary: Convert counts to physical units with the reference voltage and the sensor's transfer function, then filter the noise.
nodes.outcome: Convert a raw ADC reading to temperature for a linear sensor.
nodes.check: A sensor outputs 10 mV/°C, read by a 10-bit ADC with a 5 V reference. The reading is 61. Temperature?

nodes.label: UART Serial
nodes.summary: Asynchronous bytes framed by start and stop bits at an agreed baud rate.
nodes.outcome: Configure a UART and print debugging output.
nodes.check: At 9600 baud with 8N1 framing, roughly how many bytes per second can be sent?
nodes.answer: 960 (10 bits per byte including start and stop).

nodes.label: I²C & SPI Buses
nodes.summary: I²C: two wires, addressed devices, open-drain with pull-ups. SPI: a clock, two data lines and a chip select per device, faster.
nodes.outcome: Read a register from an I²C sensor.
nodes.check: Why do I²C lines need pull-up resistors?
nodes.answer: Devices only pull the lines low (open-drain); the resistors return them high.

nodes.label: Finite State Machines in Firmware
nodes.summary: Explicit states and transitions keep event-driven firmware understandable and testable.
nodes.outcome: Model a traffic light or debouncer as a state machine.
nodes.check: What two things fully define a finite state machine's behaviour?
nodes.answer: Its set of states and its transition rules (current state + input → next state and output).

nodes.label: RTOS & Scheduling
nodes.summary: Tasks with priorities, a scheduler, and the hazards of shared resources: deadlock and priority inversion.
nodes.outcome: Split firmware into prioritised tasks and protect shared data with a mutex.
nodes.check: What is priority inversion?
nodes.answer: A high-priority task waits on a resource held by a low-priority task, which is itself preempted by a medium-priority one.

nodes.label: Low-Power Design
nodes.summary: Sleep modes, waking on interrupts, and duty cycling to stretch a battery from days to years.
nodes.outcome: Estimate battery life from active and sleep currents.
nodes.check: A device draws 10 mA for 1 s every minute and 10 µA otherwise. Average current?

nodes.label: Hardware Debugging
nodes.summary: Multimeter, oscilloscope, logic analyser and a debugger: measure the signal before blaming the code.
nodes.outcome: Use a logic analyser to decode a failing bus transaction.
nodes.check: Your I²C sensor never answers. What is the first thing to measure?
nodes.answer: That SDA and SCL idle high (pull-ups present) and that the device address is acknowledged, using a scope or logic analyser.
